FrogFarmers is a decision-support protot: FrogFarmers is a decision-support prototype for exploring crop rotations at field level. It brings field boundaries, soil and crop information, environmental history, and rotation recommendations into one place, so farmers can compare strategies and review the actions each one proposes.
Farmers around the world navigate shifti: Farmers around the world navigate shifting temperatures, changing rainfall patterns, water shortages, extreme weather, and declining soil health. These pressures make it difficult to choose crop rotations that protect fields, conserve water, and support long-term resilience. Your challenge is to create a decision-support tool that uses NASA Earth observations along with local soil information, crop characteristics, and farmer priorities to help farmers explore rotation strategies that could strengthen soil health and adapt their farms to changing conditions.
A crop that worked well last season may: A crop that worked well last season may be less suitable as rainfall, soil moisture, and nutrient availability change. Farmers need to weigh those conditions together, understand the trade-offs between rotations, and decide when to prepare, plant, irrigate, or reassess.
The proposed workflow combines NASA Eart: The proposed workflow combines NASA Earth observations with local soil data, crop characteristics, and farmer priorities to support field-specific rotation strategies. Each strategy explains its inputs, compares current and projected conditions, and proposes actions that farmers can review before adding the schedule to their calendar.
This demo illustrates the workflow with: This demo illustrates the workflow with sample field data and predictions.
We are a six-frog team from Ukraine. We’: We are a six-frog team from Ukraine. We’ve competed in several hackathons, so we know how to scope tightly, split work cleanly and ship a working demo under pressure. Our strength is turning large, messy datasets into tools people can actually use. We care about validation as much as speed: we test our models against real data and are upfront about what they can and can’t do.

Green means healthy. Amber means a field: Green means healthy. Amber means a field needs attention. Red marks a critical metric that calls for prompt care. Each indicator includes a plain-language explanation.
